---
title: "Model Assessment and Resampling"
---

This lecture turns model fitting into model evaluation. Students learn
why training error is optimistic and how resampling estimates
out-of-sample performance.

## Learning Objectives

- Define training, validation, and test error.
- Compare validation splits, LOOCV, k-fold cross-validation, and the
  bootstrap.
- Explain the bias and variance of error estimates.
- Use resampling to select among competing models.

## Core Ideas

A model is useful only if it generalizes. Cross-validation estimates
generalization by repeatedly fitting on one part of the data and
evaluating on held-out observations.

## Worked Example

Use an auto or housing data example to compare polynomial models under
validation-set and k-fold cross-validation estimates.

## Resampling Sequence

One useful way to teach resampling is as a code-forward sequence:

1. Fit competing polynomial regression models on the `Auto` data.
2. Compare training error with validation-set error.
3. Estimate test error with leave-one-out cross-validation.
4. Repeat with k-fold cross-validation.
5. Use the bootstrap to estimate uncertainty in a statistic or model
   coefficient.

The conceptual through-line is that resampling lets us ask questions
that one fitted model cannot answer by itself.

```r
library(boot)
library(ISLR)

auto <- na.omit(ISLR::Auto)

cv_error <- function(degree) {
  fit <- glm(mpg ~ poly(horsepower, degree), data = auto)
  cv.glm(auto, fit)$delta[1]
}

sapply(1:5, cv_error)
```

The important classroom moment is not the exact numeric winner. It is
the comparison of model complexity against estimated out-of-sample
error.

## Bootstrap as Uncertainty Engine

Bootstrap examples often start with estimating the uncertainty of a
single statistic and then extend naturally to uncertainty in linear
regression coefficients. The general recipe is:

1. define the statistic of interest,
2. resample rows with replacement,
3. recompute the statistic many times,
4. summarize the bootstrap distribution.

```r
boot_lm <- function(data, index) {
  coef(lm(mpg ~ horsepower, data = data[index, ]))
}

boot(auto, boot_lm, R = 1000)
```
